skill.name: playwright-cli
skill.description: Use Playwright CLI to inspect live web pages, capture snapshots, test selectors, and prepare ScreenCI browser automation flows.
skill.summary: Inspect and automate web pages with Playwright CLI for testing and ScreenCI workflows.
skill.author: screenci

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown backticks or documented example URLs, not hidden code execution. Confirmed risks remain because the skill directs agents to run Playwright CLI and package-manager commands, including browser actions, JavaScript evaluation, file snapshots, and a global npm install. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Broad package manager commands are allowed.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed tools to the exact npm or npx commands required, and pin package versions instead of using @latest.

remediation.issue: Global installation modifies the host environment.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer project-local, pinned dependencies or require user confirmation before installing packages globally.

remediation.issue: Browser automation examples can act on real websites and submit form data.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to use staging sites and test credentials before running click, fill, or submit workflows against live services.

remediation.issue: playwright-cli eval can run arbitrary page-context JavaScript.
remediation.suggestion: Limit examples to read-only inspections and caution against evaluating untrusted or state-changing scripts.

content.user_title: Inspect Web Pages with Playwright CLI
content.value_statement: Browser test setup can fail when selectors, consent banners, or page flows are unclear. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Playwright CLI inspection and repeatable automation steps.
actual_capabilities: Open a browser session and navigate to a target URL with playwright-cli.
Capture page snapshots with element references for selector discovery.
Click, type, fill, select, check, hover, and press keys in a browser page.
Evaluate page or element JavaScript expressions through Playwright CLI.
Manage named browser sessions and close individual or all sessions.
Compare raw snapshots before and after an interaction.
limitations: Requires playwright-cli or a local package installation to be available.
Needs network access for live page navigation.
Does not replace a full Playwright test suite or assertion framework.
Browser actions can change real pages, so use test accounts and safe environments.

use_cases.title: Prepare ScreenCI Browser Flows
use_cases.description: Inspect a live site, find stable selectors, and plan hidden setup steps before writing a ScreenCI script.

use_cases.title: Debug Web Test Selectors
use_cases.description: Capture snapshots and test locators when a browser test fails or a page structure changes.

use_cases.title: Explore Frontend Interaction Paths
use_cases.description: Navigate pages, click controls, and compare snapshots to understand how an interface changes.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open a browser with playwright-cli, go to [URL], take a snapshot, and summarize the main page sections and visible buttons.

prompt_templates.title: Find Stable Selectors
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [URL] with playwright-cli. Find stable selectors for the sign-in flow and identify any cookie consent step.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Interaction Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Use playwright-cli snapshots to compare the page before and after clicking [control]. Report changed regions and likely selectors.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a ScreenCI Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a ScreenCI setup plan for [URL] using playwright-cli. Include hidden consent handling, session steps, and selectors for the visible demo.

output_examples.input: Inspect a login page and find the safest selector for the submit action.
output_examples.output: A concise report with the page title, consent banner action, submit control selector, and recommended next inspection step.

output_examples.input: Compare a product page before and after opening the cart drawer.
output_examples.output: A change summary that names the drawer region, key controls, updated text, and selectors suitable for a test.

output_examples.input: Prepare a ScreenCI flow for a marketing page with a cookie banner.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline with hidden consent handling, visible demo steps, and notes about selectors that may be fragile.

best_practices: Use staging URLs or test accounts before running actions that submit forms.
Review snapshots after each major action before writing selectors into tests.
Close browser sessions when the workflow is complete.
anti_patterns: Do not run package installation commands without confirming the package source and version.
Do not enter production credentials into unknown or third-party pages.
Do not rely on brittle positional selectors when accessible roles or test IDs are available.

faq.question: Does this skill install Playwright CLI automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains npx and npm commands, but the user or agent must decide whether to run them.

faq.question: Can it test private applications?
faq.answer: Yes, if the browser session can access the application and you have permission.

faq.question: Does it write Playwright test files?
faq.answer: It helps discover flows and selectors. A separate coding step can turn the findings into tests.

faq.question: Can it handle cookie banners?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks the agent to inspect and record consent actions for hidden setup steps.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What are the main safety concerns?
faq.answer: It can run browser and package manager commands, navigate websites, and submit form data.
